skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At the very start (T2) the interviewer stated: "we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice."

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains that the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and disclose what is learned "without your consent and without telling you."

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 sets out how the interview will proceed, asks for complete answers, explains that speculation must be flagged, and asks the witness to say whether they remember or are reconstructing.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asks the witness to restate who is represented and who controls privilege, and T2 and T6 invite questions; the restatement at T5 shows the warning was understood.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T356 covers keeping documents, confidentiality, not discussing with witnesses, and 'Anything to add or correct?', but next steps are thin ('We may follow up').

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
The company decides whether to waive it, and it may disclose what we learn, including to the government, without your consent and without telling you.
Before we go on, could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
Explains how the interview will proceed and sets ground rules: flag speculation, assumptions and estimates, say whether something is remembered or reconstructed, and ask for clarification.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up. Anything to add or correct?

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Opens broadly with 'Tell me everything you remember' at T16, T44 and T80 and lets the witness walk through events before probing.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Generally moves from role and process to specific transactions and documents, though some topics such as the Raptor returns jump between general and specific.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are clear and single-focused, e.g. T56 and T346, but some are compound or long, such as the T2 warning and T278.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Remains neutral and polite throughout, using phrasing like 'Help me understand how those fit together' at T252 and T306 without becoming confrontational.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Departs from the outline to pursue the Southampton investment, the Chewco note and the Raptor minutes when answers warranted, though some answers were left unexplored.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how Chewco came to be formed in 1997.
How do you know they reviewed every transaction?
How did those reviews work in practice? Take a specific deal.
Did you consider whether the Board should know that LJM2's returns were several times what it had been told?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Follows up on evasions such as 'I don't believe it came up' at T163 and the 'tremendous utilization' statement at T252, but lets some answers pass, such as 'perfectly capable' at T107.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Systematically pins down who, what, when and how, for example the Foundation's $4.5M return on a set date (T142) and the Chewco figure moving from $1M to $10M (T278-T282).

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Asks what could help the witness remember (T62) and shows the minutes (T70) and documents, though it does not use every available route.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Repeatedly separates personal knowledge from hearsay, e.g. T56 'How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?' and T346 'did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?'

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: Asks who else to speak with (T336, T338) and identifies Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper and McMahon as additional witnesses.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: Asks about minutes (T62), foundation statements (T350), and the witness's personal notes and emails (T352-T355), and asks where the deal files are kept (T348).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Asks how certain the witness is of the $4.5M figure (T144), the $229M figure (T222) and the approximate return (T118), and whether the timing is known (T318).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Follows up on most material responses, such as the Southampton terms (T156-T158) and the 'may have said it should be resolved' answer (T332), but some answers are not followed up, such as 'perfectly capable' (T107).

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
What's your best estimate?
How certain are you of that figure?
The minutes record you saying there had been "tremendous utilization" of Raptor I. Our information is that Talon hadn't yet done any derivatives with Enron. Help me understand how those fit together.
How did it go from about $1 million to about $10 million?
Earlier you told me you stayed out of the Chewco buyout. This note, addressed to "Andy," refers to $10.5 million for the buyout. Help me understand how those fit together.
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
How do you know that: did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?
Do you have any personal files, notes, or emails about LJM, Chewco, or Southampton?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Introduces each document with context and authenticates it, e.g. the Southampton agreement's signature block (T134-T135) and the Chewco note's handwriting (T300-T303).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Gets the witness's account first, e.g. asks for returns before showing the October 2000 report (T192-T194) and asks about Southampton before showing the agreement (T126-T128).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Describes documents accurately and consistent with the record, e.g. the $4.5M on $25,000 with a May 1, 2000 distribution (T142) and the quoted 'was not at risk' language (T260).

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Mostly neutral framing, but T210 'whether the Board should know that LJM2's returns were several times what it had been told' presents a conclusion rather than an open question.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: Gives the witness fair opportunities to reconcile differences, e.g. T252-T253, T306-T307 and T332-T333 'Is that fair?'

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
Our information is that on May 1, 2000, about six weeks after it invested, the Foundation received roughly $4.5 million on its $25,000. Is that accurate?
It says their return "was not at risk" because LJM2 "had already received its return of and on capital." Is that what you told them?
I'm not suggesting you wrote it. Do you recognize it?
So your account is that you don't recall authorizing the payment, and you may have asked that it be resolved after counsel advised there was no basis for it. Is that fair?

missed_opportunities: T107: The witness says Glisan reported to him but 'was perfectly capable of representing Enron's interests.' The interviewer did not follow up on the conflict of a subordinate negotiating against the CFO's partnership, which bears directly on the approval controls.

T51: The witness says 'Our lawyers advised' that a senior officer's participation would require proxy disclosure and Code approval. The interviewer did not ask which lawyers advised this, when, or whether the advice was in writing, though it was central to why Kopper was chosen.
tips: When the witness says 'I may have' or 'I don't recall' about a specific act, such as a payment authorization or a call, ask: 'What, if anything, in your own notes, emails or calendar would confirm that, and when would you expect to find it?'
When the witness relies on advice from others, such as 'Our lawyers advised,' ask: 'Who gave that advice, when, in what form, and what exactly did they say?'
